chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from al-Nadr from 'Asim from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who hires a slave and the slave consumes a large amount of wealth, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability on his master, and it is not for them to sell him, but he should be asked to compensate (from his own earnings). If he is unable to compensate, there is no liability on the master and no liability on the slave.'

key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: he is asked to compensate (from his own earnings)

ai.seo_question: What is the financial ruling when a hired slave wastes his master's money?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *istis'a* (seeking ability) in commercial contracts, establishing that the master bears no residual liability if the hired slave exhausts the capital, provided the slave is not sold to cover the debt. It highlights the Shia juristic view that financial responsibility in such partnerships rests on the agent's capacity to repay from future earnings rather than asset liquidation, reflecting a nuanced approach to risk allocation in pre-modern economic transactions.
